p.t: In short
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t: For almost every account, use **standard attribution** (the rule that decides which sales an ad gets credit for), not incremental attribution.
Only keep the **7-day click window. Set engaged-view and view-through to None**.
Attribution settings lock once something is published, so **check them before you press Publish**.
From **May 2026**, new campaigns use **7-day click plus 1-day engage-through**, set at ad set level.
Do not change a live ad set's setting. Build a new campaign and move over slowly.
Attribution settings for standard setups: Standard vs. incremental attribution
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t: **Standard attribution is the setting for nearly all accounts.**
**Attribution means the rule that decides which ad gets credit for a sale. Meta selects engaged-view by default. Engaged-view counts a sale from someone who watched an ad without clicking it.**
**Change that default to None** to keep only the 7-day click window.
**Incremental attribution** uses more complex models to estimate whether an ad caused a conversion. A conversion is a sale or other goal action. Standard attribution uses the click and view windows.
A window is the number of days after a click or view that still counts. Standard attribution is the choice for nearly all accounts. Incremental attribution is only worth testing in specific cases.
For a **CBO test ad set, keep Customer life cycle strategy on Get conversions from all audiences**. CBO (campaign budget optimization) means Meta shares one budget across the ad sets in a campaign.
Keep the **Attribution model on Standard**. The conversion event stays on **Purchase**.
1. Open the ad set and go to **Show more settings**.
p.h: Setting standard attribution step by step

p.t:
2. Under Attribution setting, click the **pencil (the edit icon) and select Standard attribution**, not Incremental attribution.
3. Open Standard attribution selections with its pencil.
4. Change the default of 7-day click, 1-day engaged-view, 1-day view to **7-day click only**.
5. Set **Engaged-view to None and View-through to None**. View-through counts a sale from someone who saw an ad without clicking or engaging.
**Attribution settings can only be changed before a campaign or ad set is published.** Once published, they are locked.
The only fix is to duplicate the item and start over. That is why you must check the settings before pressing Publish.
Meta attribution can arrive **days late**.
p.h: Attribution windows: 7-Day click vs. engage-Through: Why the window matters for reading data

p.t: When this was written, the attribution window was 7 days. A sale can appear after a campaign was switched off. The start date in the campaign name helps you read the data correctly.
What changed on march 17, 2026: The change in reporting
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t: On **March 17, 2026**, Meta redefined its attribution settings.
The same ad performance is now reported differently. No new attribution windows were added. Ads Manager (Meta's ad dashboard) shows a grey notice at the top of the account about this change.
**Before March 17**, click-through attribution counted any interaction with an ad.
That included link clicks, likes, comments, saves, shares, story swipe-ups, Shop Now clicks, and clicks on carousels or dynamic catalog ads. A carousel is an ad with several swipeable images.
Dynamic catalog ads show products from your product feed.
**After the change**, click-through only counts real clicks. All other interactions moved into engage-through.
Engage-through now covers all engagement types, such as likes, comments, saves and shares. Engaged-view counts an ad view longer than a set time limit.
That limit is reportedly around **six to seven seconds**, but this figure still needs confirmation.
Revenue moved from click-through into engage-through.
Accounts that only report click-through saw conversions and revenue **drop overnight**. The ad performance itself did not change.
Some accounts still report noticeably less revenue on click-through than before the update.

**Adding click-through and engage-through together** gives a number close to what was reported before March 17. That is why the combined setting became the new reference for evergreen account structures.
Evergreen means a long-running setup that is not tied to one short promotion.
Recommended settings after the change
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t: **New campaigns from May 2026**
Recommended setting: 7-day click plus 1-day engage-through

Notes: Set at ad set level. The 7-day click window was previously the only setting in use.
**Many accounts after the March 2026 redefinition**
Recommended setting: 1-day click plus 1-day engage-through
Notes: Came closest to the performance previously reported by 7-day click alone. Reported numbers stayed slightly above historical levels even with this setting.
**Recommended setting for new campaigns from May 2026: 7-day click plus 1-day engage-through.** It is set at ad set level. The 7-day click window was previously the only setting in use.
After Meta's March 2026 redefinition, data from many accounts showed that **1-day click plus 1-day engage-through** came closest to the performance previously reported by 7-day click alone.
Even with this combined setting, reported numbers stayed slightly above the historical levels.
**You cannot change the attribution setting of a published ad set.**
p.h: Transition Rules: Principles for changing live accounts

p.t: **So an existing asset cannot simply be switched to 7-day click plus 1-day engage-through. An asset means any ad set or campaign. The transition has to be done with new ad sets or campaigns**.

**Do not switch the whole ad account at once. That resets the learning phase of every asset and causes a large performance drop. The learning phase is the period when Meta tests an ad set to find buyers.**
**The transition should happen gradually over a longer period**.
**Do not put an ad set with a new setting into the same CBO campaign as ad sets with the old setting. Meta moves most of the budget to the ad set with more attributed conversions.**
**Test the new setting in a separate campaign** instead.
Transition plan by account type
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t:
**Satisfied with performance**
Pace: Slow, new campaign runs alongside the old one

Planned timeline: About **six months**
Reason: Little urgency, so the risk of a large drop is avoided.
**Break-even**

Pace: Bigger changes acceptable
Planned timeline: Short
Reason: Performance was weak to begin with, so there is little to lose.

**Losing money on first order**
Pace: Fast switch with a short overlap
Planned timeline: About **three days** of overlap
Reason: Little to lose, so bigger changes are acceptable.
1. Keep the existing campaign running with its current attribution setting.
p.h: Transition procedure for a satisfied account

p.t: 2. Create a new campaign that uses **7-day click plus 1-day engage-through** at ad set level.
3. Launch all new ad sets and every new batch of creative **only in the new campaign**. Never add the new setting to the existing campaign.
4. Keep the original campaign running for as long as it produces a **positive contribution margin** (profit left after the direct costs of a sale). Let the new campaign take over gradually.
5. Plan for a transition period of about **six months**.
1. **Duplicate** the entire campaign that is currently running.
p.h: Transition procedure for an account losing money on first order

p.t:
2. Switch the duplicate to **7-day click plus 1-day engage-through**.
3. Run the original and the duplicate side by side for about **three days**.
4. Once the new campaign outperforms the old one, which usually happens almost immediately, **turn off the original campaign**.
5. Run only the new campaign from then on. Send all new ad sets into it.
**Copy the current campaign. In the copy, change every attribution setting to 7-day click plus 1-day engage-through**.
p.h: Transition procedure for a break-Even account

p.t: Load all the new creative into that copy. From then on, treat the new campaign as the account's structure.

Another route is to copy the best-performing ad sets into a **fresh campaign** with the correct setting. Or start new ad sets inside the existing campaign with that setting. Meta will favor the new ad sets.
That is fine here, because performance was weak to begin with.
Incremental attribution (Older advice, 2025 onward): What It Is
p.s: Attribution settings and the march 2026 changes

p.t: Incremental attribution is an optimization option available since around **October**
**or November 2025**. It aims at incremental conversions, meaning sales that would not have happened without the ad.
It uses machine learning (software that learns patterns from data) to predict whether an ad caused a purchase.
After the March 2026 change, incremental reporting was higher than 7-day click in some accounts. That made it worth testing.
A purchase from someone who had **never seen the brand before counts as incremental. A buyer who had already visited the site, added to cart, or was on the email list is unlikely to count.**
**So results depend heavily on how many returning customers** reach the account.
Some accounts show an option at ad set level to optimize **purely for new customers** under incremental attribution.
Incremental optimization worked well for large brands that already optimize for incrementality. It performed poorly for many smaller accounts when it first appeared in late 2025.
Its results depend on how many returning customers the account already receives. **Test it before you rely on it.**
1. Create a **separate campaign** with your best-performing evergreen ad sets.

2. Run it with **7-day click plus 1-day engage-through** as the optimization setting.
3. Note the incremental number that comes out of the campaign.
4. Break down **new customer ROAS** (return on ad spend, meaning revenue per dollar spent, counted only for new buyers) by audience segment and by spend split.
5. **Keep incremental only if** it produces a better new customer ROAS than the 7-day click plus 1-day engage-through campaign.
**Customer lifecycle strategy sits at ad set level, near the top of the screen. It offers Acquire new customers with exclusions**.
p.h: Customer lifecycle settings: Where the Settings Are

p.t: For example, it can exclude buyers from the last **180 days**, using the pixel (Meta's tracking code on your site) and an existing customer list.
To tell Meta which buyers count as existing customers, open **Account settings** and scroll down to the existing customers section.
Once this is set, the campaign reports the **split between new and existing customers**.
**Customer lifecycle strategy has shown poor results as of May 29, 2026.** It is not recommended for acquiring new customers.
Incremental attribution is the better option to test for that goal.
